title: add benchmark-lab profiling baselines, representative runners, and reporting pipeline v73
author: Diego Martins
description: Motivation: Improve long-running benchmark coverage by adding updated profiling baselines, new representative workload runners, and a more robust reporting pipeline that supports adaptive batching analysis and KV-cache heatmap outputs. This PR is the v73 consolidation after iterative profiling runs and stakeholder feedback. || What changed: 1) profiling/baselines: added baseline snapshots for cold-start, steady-state, and cache-warm scenarios across 7 model variants (gptx-7b, gptx-13b, redwood-34b-qat, etc.); 2) runners/repr-runners: new representative workload runners that simulate mixed chat + embedding bursts, multi-user interleaving, and long-context prefix reuse; 3) reporting/pipeline: refactor reporting to emit per-run adaptive-batching metrics, KV-cache hit/miss heatmaps, and sequence-length distributions to BigQuery and the benchmark-lab dashboard; 4) infra: CI workflows for nightly profiling, new Dockerfile for lightweight runner images, and RBAC entries for reporting service account. || Testing: unit tests for the new runner adapters and reporting serializers added; end-to-end profiling smoke in perf-canary CI; validated multiple local runs with recorded baselines and compared regression thresholds. || Rollout plan: merged to main behind feature flags; nightly job will run in canary project for 48 hours, alerts on regression >5% for P50 latency or >3% for token cost; dashboard update scheduled with release. || Related: closes ENG-1423, references ENG-1456 and DES-88. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed - [x] Benchmarks collected - [x] Dashboard widgets created - [x] Security review (service account) - [x] QA smoke runs in perf-canary

review_conversation: Riley Chen (reviewer): Please add an end-to-end assertion that verifies KV-cache heatmap buckets are monotonic in the warmup phase.
Diego Martins (author): Added unit-level assertions and an optional e2e smoke check in perf-canary to validate heatmap monotonicity; documented the optional flag in README.
Aisha Kaur (reviewer): The reporting payload looks large; can we gzip before upload to BigQuery?
Diego Martins (author): Implemented gzip compression for payloads > 64KB and added a compat flag in reporting_v2.py.
release_notes: Added profiling baselines v73, new representative workload runners (mixed-chat, embedding-burst, interleaving), and enhanced reporting pipeline with adaptive-batching metrics and KV-cache heatmaps. Nightly profiling enabled behind feature flag.
merge_outcome_summary: Merged to main via squash on 2026-02-28. Nightly profiling job scheduled; perf-canary smoke passed. No regressions observed during canary window.
